ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ is obtained through a similarity transformation from the regular hexagon $A^{\prime}B^{\prime}C^{\prime}D^{\prime}E^{\prime}F^{\prime}$. Given that $AB=3$ and $B^{\prime}C^{\prime}=1$, what is the ratio of the area of the regular hexagon $A^{\prime}B^{\prime}C^{\prime}D^{\prime}E^{\prime}F^{\prime}$ to that of the regular hexagon $ABCDEF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the hexagon $ABCDEF$ is obtained from the hexagon $A'B'C'D'E'F'$ through a similarity transformation,\\
thus hexagon $ABCDEF \sim$ hexagon $A'B'C'D'E'F'$,\\
hence, the ratio of the areas of the hexagons $A'B'C'D'E'F'$ to $ABCDEF$ is equal to $(1\colon 3)^{2}=\boxed{1\colon 9}$.
